title: Authentication Flows & Token Refresh
description: Implement authentication flows with automatic token refresh using React Query interceptors and mutations.

data.text: Modern web applications almost always require authentication. React Query is well-suited for managing auth state because it understands loading, error, and success states natively. In this lesson, you will learn how to implement a complete authentication flow with automatic token refresh using React Query mutations and query invalidation.

data.title: Common Auth Problems
items: Access tokens expire and cause 401 errors on active queries
Users see unexpected loading spinners when tokens refresh
Race conditions between multiple simultaneous requests
Refreshing the token too often wastes API resources
Storing tokens securely across client-side routes

data.title: Security Warning
data.text: Never store access tokens or refresh tokens in localStorage. Use secure, HTTP-only cookies whenever possible, or encrypted session storage if cookies are not an option.

data.caption: Complete authentication flow with token refresh lifecycle
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant Q as React Query
    participant A as Auth API
    participant P as Protected API

    C->>A: Login with credentials
    A-->>C: accessToken + refreshToken
    C->>Q: Store tokens in QueryClient defaults

    loop Every request
        C->>P: Request with accessToken
        alt Token valid
            P-->>C: Data response
        else Token expired (401)
            P-->>C: 401 Unauthorized
            C->>Q: Pause all queries
            C->>A: Refresh token request
            A-->>C: New accessToken
            C->>Q: Resume queries, retry failed
            C->>P: Retry original request
            P-->>C: Data response
        end
    end

data.title: useRefreshToken Mutation
data.content: Create a mutation to handle token refresh. This mutation will be called automatically when a 401 is detected.

data.title: Optimistic Token Refresh
data.text: Use onMutate to immediately update the auth state before the API call completes. If the refresh fails, use onError to roll back to the previous state.

data.title: Global 401 Handler
data.content: Set up a global fetch wrapper or queryFn that intercepts 401 responses and triggers a token refresh before retrying.

data.title: Auth Flow Steps
items: User submits credentials via login mutation
Store both access and refresh tokens securely
Include access token in all subsequent requests
When 401 occurs, pause active queries and refresh token
Update token storage and retry failed queries
If refresh fails, redirect to login and clear state

data.title: Login Mutation with Auth Setup
data.content: Complete login flow that stores tokens and initializes auth state.

data.title: Protected Query Hook
data.content: Create a reusable hook for protected API calls that automatically handles token refresh.

items.hint: Use HTTP-only cookies or encrypted storage

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use useMutation for login and token refresh operations
Store tokens securely, not in localStorage
Handle 401 errors globally to provide seamless UX
Use enabled flag to prevent queries when not authenticated
Always clear cache and tokens on logout
data.takeaway: Authentication with React Query requires careful coordination between mutations, queries, and token management.
